data.name: Arjil
data.gender_notes: Arjil is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arjil is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Indra', the Hindu god of rain and thunder. This name is believed to bring the power and strength of Indra to the one who bears it. Arjil is a revered name in Hindu culture, symbolizing the divine power of nature and the courage of its bearer. The name Arjil carries the meaning “Lord of the Thunderbolt” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arjil usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the thunderbolt and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a person who is devoted to the truth and follows the righteous path.
data.etymology: Arjil belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Thunderbolt.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arjil total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference:
Arjuna, also known as Arjil in some regional texts, was a central character in the Indian epic Mahabharata, which is estimated to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.
Context: Arjuna was a great warrior and a key member of the Pandava dynasty. He was mentored by Bhagavad Gita, the divine discourse delivered by Lord Krishna, which became a foundational text of Hinduism.

According to some Jain texts, Arjil was a Jain Tirthankara who lived between the 11th and 10th centuries BCE. In Jain tradition, Tirthankaras are enlightened beings who serve as teachers and guides for the spiritual development of the community.
Context: Arjil is described as a prince from the Videha kingdom, who renounced worldly pleasures to embark on a spiritual journey, eventually attaining omniscience and liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
